matching_policy.ambiguous: Leave the processor blank when two source processors can explain the same plotted marker.
known_discrepancies: Xeon E5-2699 v3 chart 140 W versus source 145 W
digitized graph x-coordinates versus documented dates
Xeon W5580 graph 36.6 versus cited SPEC result 36.7
matching_policy.legacy_second_pass: Require agreement across at least three metric fields within a tight graph-year cluster and reject non-unique core-count overlaps.
matching_policy.validated_export: Include only direct and high-confidence named rows whose plotted value is source-supported; exclude unresolved rows and approved graph/source conflicts.

cornell-mips-r2000-1986-01-01.notes: A 16.67 MHz R2000 system has a published early SPEC integer result, but no defensible conversion from that pre-SPEC92 result to the chart's normalized SPECint2006-equivalent scale was found.

cornell-amd-am486-1993-03-01.notes: The source identifies only the Am486 family at 40 MHz. Published SPECint92 material does not identify a sufficiently specific AMD model and system configuration for a defensible assignment.

cornell-amd-k5-1996-03-01.notes: Contemporary sources publish estimated SPECint92 targets for K5, not a verified result for the exact 90 MHz record, and no defensible cross-suite conversion was found.

cornell-sun-ultrasparc-t1-niagara-2005-0.notes: No published SPEC CPU integer speed or rate result was found for the 1.2 GHz UltraSPARC T1. Other integer and web-server benchmarks are not convertible to SPECint.

cornell-amd-turion-64-x2-mt-40-lancaster.notes: The source record conflicts internally: MT-40 Lancaster is a 2.2 GHz single-core part, while the row says two cores. A nearby TL-60 result cannot safely be assigned to this ambiguous identity.

cornell-ibm-cell-2007-05-05.notes: Cell combines one control-oriented PPE with eight specialized SPEs. No official SPECint result for this heterogeneous configuration was found, and its floating-point throughput is not convertible to SPECint.

cornell-sun-ultrasparc-t2-niagara-2-2007.basis: SPECint_rate2006 peak divided by physical cores
cornell-sun-ultrasparc-t2-niagara-2-2007.notes: Estimated as 78.5 / 8 physical cores = 9.8125 for the matching 1.417 GHz UltraSPARC T2 system. This is a per-core throughput proxy, not a submitted SPECint2006 speed result.

cornell-amd-phenom-9600-2007-09-01.notes: No official Phenom 9600 submission was found. The value uses an official 2.3 GHz AMD Opteron 2356 result from the same K10/Barcelona generation as a system-level proxy.

cornell-amd-phenom-x3-8850-2008-10-01.notes: No official Phenom X3 8850 submission was found. The value uses an official 2.5 GHz AMD Opteron 2360 SE result from the same K10 generation as a system-level proxy.

cornell-intel-dunnington-x7460-2009-04-0.notes: Official SPEC CPU2006 integer speed result for the exact Intel Xeon X7460 at 2.66 GHz.

cornell-intel-gainestown-w5580-2009-04-0.notes: Official SPEC CPU2006 integer speed result for the exact Intel Xeon W5580 at 3.20 GHz.

cornell-sun-rock-2009-09-01.notes: Rock was cancelled before commercial release. No validated production-system SPECint result exists for a defensible assignment.

newdata-power7-780-2012-08.basis: SPECint_rate2006 peak divided by physical cores
newdata-power7-780-2012-08.notes: Estimated as 4140 / 128 physical cores = 32.34375. This is a per-core throughput proxy, not a submitted SPECint2006 speed result.

newdata-xeon-phi-2013-05.notes: The repository names only the Xeon Phi family, not a unique model. No defensible single-thread SPECint value was assigned.

newdata-power8-s814-2014-06.basis: SPECint_rate2006 peak divided by physical cores
newdata-power8-s814-2014-06.notes: Estimated as 261 / 4 physical cores = 65.25. This is a per-core throughput proxy from the matching S814 system, not a submitted SPECint2006 speed result.

newdata-xeon-phi-7290-2016-06.basis: SPECint_rate2006 peak divided by physical cores
newdata-xeon-phi-7290-2016-06.notes: Estimated as 1220 / 72 physical cores = 16.944. This is a per-core throughput proxy and is sensitive to the four hardware threads used per core.

newdata-power8-2016-08.basis: SPECint_rate2006 peak divided by physical cores
newdata-power8-2016-08.notes: The generic 4.0 GHz POWER8 entry is matched to the 4.0 GHz Power E880 result and estimated as 14400 / 192 physical cores = 75.0.

newdata-epyc-7601-2017-06.notes: Converted from the official SPECspeed2017_int peak score using the repository's documented 9.0 cross-suite factor: 7.33 x 9 = 65.97.

newdata-power9-ac922-2018-04.basis: POWER9 SPECrate2017_int peak per physical core multiplied by 9
newdata-power9-ac922-2018-04.notes: No AC922 integer speed submission was found. Estimated from the same-frequency POWER9 S924 result: (277 / 24 physical cores) x 9 = 103.875.

newdata-quadro-gv100-2018-05.notes: Not applicable: GPU floating-point throughput cannot be converted into a CPU SPECint single-thread score.

newdata-m1-2020-09.notes: Converted from AnandTech's estimated SPECint2017 single-thread score using the repository's 9.0 factor: 6.66 x 9 = 59.94. This was not an official SPEC submission.

newdata-m1-max-2021-08.basis: M1 SPECint2017 single-thread proxy multiplied by 9
newdata-m1-max-2021-08.notes: AnandTech found M1 Max single-thread performance changed little from M1 because both use 3.23 GHz Firestorm cores. The M1 converted value, 6.66 x 9 = 59.94, is used as a proxy.

newdata-graviton-3-2021-09.notes: AWS publishes relative estimated SPECint2017 rate improvements, but no absolute single-thread score suitable for the chart's conversion was found.

newdata-radeon-mi250-2021-09.notes: Not applicable: GPU floating-point throughput cannot be converted into a CPU SPECint single-thread score.
